title: Tenant lanes, enforced soft/hard quotas, and noisy-neighbor throttles for Dedicated GPU fleets
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: implement tenant 'lanes' (logical GPU capacity partitions), an enforceable two-tier quota model (soft throttles + hard limits), and automated noisy-neighbor mitigation primitives that integrate with autoscaling and our existing scheduling runtime. This work will give Dedicated customers predictable throughput guarantees while protecting multi-tenant hosts from single-tenant interference.

Background: customers running reserved capacity have asked for stronger isolation guarantees beyond simple slot reservations. We've seen several incidents where aggressive KV-cache/memory-heavy tenants consumed GPU upload bandwidth and NVLink, causing p99 latency spikes for other tenants on the same nodes. Existing mitigations (soft soft-quota alerts, manual burst pools) are insufficient for predictable SLAs.

Scope and deliverables:
- Design and implement tenant lanes: lightweight logical partitions applied at scheduler time that assign tenants a combination of: guaranteed GPU lanes (fractional GPU or MIG-based partitions where available), bandwidth/PCIe NVLink egress tokens, and priority class.
- Two-tier quota enforcement: soft throttles (token-bucket rate limit + dynamic backpressure to clients) and hard limits that reject new requests when the tenant exceeds its hard quota for sustained periods. Soft throttles will integrate with SDK error codes and advisory headers so clients can adapt (Retry-After semantics).
- Noisy neighbor mitigation primitives: (a) automatic throttling when tenant per-node p99 latency or GPU utilization delta crosses threshold, (b) lightweight preemption of best-effort tasks, (c) temporary placement of the noisy tenant into a constrained lane (reduced burst headroom) while alarms are investigated.
- Autoscaling interplay: define autoscaler policies per-lane. Autoscaling should preferentially grow a tenant's dedicated pool before spilling to shared headroom; conversely, when noise is detected, autoscaler will refuse to add shared nodes until tenant's soft quota is enforced.
- Observability & alerts: per-tenant metrics (p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens_consumed, hard_quota_hits, eviction_count), dashboards in Grafana, and alert rules for SRE and Account Owners.
- Rollout plan and migration tooling: canary rollout to two Dedicated clusters, tooling to migrate tenants between lanes with zero downtime where possible, operator CLI to manually escalate/revert.

Design trade-offs considered:
- Per-GPU fractional lanes (MIG) vs node-level isolation: MIG provides stronger hardware-level isolation but is limited to newer GPU families and complicates model placement. We will support both: prefer MIG when available, fall back to software cgroup-like enforcement for other hardware.
- Soft throttles vs immediate hard limits: soft throttles preserve availability and let clients gracefully degrade; hard limits are necessary for SLA protection. We'll default to soft-first, escalate to hard after sustained abuse.
- Autoscaling before placement vs placement then autoscaling: to minimize noisy neighbor risk, placement will consider current lane headroom and only trigger autoscale when lane-level quotas indicate sustained need. This increases latency to scale up slightly but prevents broad cross-tenant impact.

Implementation notes (high level):
- Scheduler hook: new LaneAllocator module that annotates placements with lane_id, lane_guarantee, lane_burst. Lane metadata will be persisted in our placement DB and surfaced to runtime agents.
- Runtime enforcement: per-tenant token-bucket placed in the request admission path; kernel-level GPU isolation where MIG is used; lightweight cgroup-like watcher to track memory and PCIe bandwidth pressure and emit signals to the LaneController.
- Autoscaler changes: policy engine extended with per-lane SLO objectives. Autoscaler will support 'headroom_pool' concept (shared nodes reserved for brief bursts) and 'hard-cutoff' Boolean to stop scaling that would otherwise spread noisy tenants.
- Metrics/telemetry: Prometheus exporters emitting tenant-lane metrics, Grafana dashboards, and an Alertmanager rule set for escalation.

Acceptance criteria:
- Can create lanes for a tenant and assign guarantees and burst headroom via Console/API.
- Soft throttles tested end-to-end: client receives 429-like advisory with Retry-After, server emits tokens_consumed metric and SRE alert when thresholds cross.
- Hard limits enforceable and reversible via operator CLI.
- Noisy neighbor scenario tests: running synthetic noisy workload demonstrates measurable reduction in collateral p99 on co-located tenants by >= 80% compared to baseline.

Rollout and migration plan:
1) Internal QA cluster runbook + synthetic noisy neighbor suite (week 1)
2) Canary on 2 Dedicated clusters with low-traffic customers (week 2)
3) Gradual ramp (10% -> 50% -> 100%) by cluster over 4 weeks, with automatic rollback on defined SLO regressions (p99 increase > 10% for tenants not being throttled).

Links and artifacts:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/Dedicated+Lanes+Quotas+Design
- Noisy neighbor test harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/noise-harness/pulls/124
- Scheduler prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/9812
- Grafana dashboard (template): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/8K4hjf/tenant-lanes
- Incident postmortem that motivated this: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1-noisy-neighbor-incident

Open questions / risks:
- How to present Retry-After semantics across SDKs consistently; needs SDK work for backoff guidance.
- MIG availability across regions: some Dedicated customers request MIG guarantees but hardware inventory is heterogeneous. Need to coordinate with procurement and DOCS to set correct expectations.
- False positives for noisy detection could reduce customer experience; tuning thresholds and a short investigation window is critical.

Next steps (this ticket):
- Finalize LaneAllocator API (ETA: 2026-03-14).
- Implement token-bucket admission and basic soft throttle in runtime (ETA: 2026-03-28).
- Wire basic Grafana dashboards and alerting (ETA: 2026-03-20).

Owner notes: This is cross-functional: runtime, scheduler, autoscaler, and console teams must coordinate. I'll host a sync and publish the API/spec once LaneAllocator draft is ready.
